item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"López Obrador acknowledged that Alejandro Encinas was spied on but denied that the Army was responsible, told Encinas not to give the matter importance, and said nobody should be spied on; the report said the Mexican Army bought Pegasus in 2019 to spy on activists and journalists and that Encinas was surveilled while investigating alleged abuses by the armed forces.","notes":["The excerpt supports the Army’s purchase of Pegasus and reported surveillance, but not the broader attribution to unspecified military institutions as established fact."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 6,060-agent deployment, the cited failures and crash involving one death and 106 injuries, López Obrador’s sabotage concern, his criticism of human-rights organizations, and his defense of expanded military participation in public security."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the reported 2022 press-violence figures, executive stigmatizing comments, advertising concentration, military opacity and espionage concerns, weak justice outcomes, pending appointments, and CNDH partiality."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the FGR investigation and 14 bullet wounds, the video’s apparent depiction of soldiers shooting the men, forensic consistency with the military account despite conflicting indications, and López Obrador’s isolated-event framing."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 8–3 ruling, the specified forms of transferred control, the constitutional civilian requirement, Morena’s stated respect despite disagreement, and the administration’s prior military-security measures."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Journalist Nelson Matus Peña was shot and killed by unidentified assailants in Acapulco on 15 July 2023; his news portal covered crime, violence, and insecurity. CPJ called for investigation of a possible retaliatory motive, reported no response from the Guerrero prosecutor’s office and the federal protection mechanism, characterized Mexican authorities as ineffective in protecting journalists, and noted Mexico’s sixth-place 2022 impunity ranking.","notes":["The excerpt says Matus’s portal covered crime and violence, but does not establish that he personally was reporting on those subjects at the time of his killing."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the reported criminal proceedings, vague offenses, stigmatization, harassment, excessive force, threats, failures to investigate violations, the National Guard protest-monitoring concern, and Amnesty’s recommendations."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the federal suspension for missing land-use authorization, prior environmental-authorization suspensions, the restart without an explicit judicial order under a national-security rationale, the listed environmental impacts, and the 2,249-hectare jaguar reserve announcement."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"López Obrador planned late-2023 inaugurations for the Tulum airport, Maya Train, and Interoceanic Corridor, while an Army-run medicine distribution center was also announced; he supervised final Maya Train work and scheduled reviews of public works. The projects involved military construction or operation, and the article reported an airport investment and critics’ concerns about symbolic, election-timed inaugurations before completion, citing Dos Bocas’s delayed start of fuel production.","notes":["The excerpt does not support that López Obrador personally supervised all the major projects or that all involved large public investments."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 13.262-billion-peso proposed cuts, the specified judiciary, INE, legislative, Auditoría, Cofece, and INAI reductions, increased allocations to executive ministries and Pemex, and the absence of an Otis-recovery allocation in the distributed draft."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0010-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"During López Obrador’s first four years, information requests and complaints over inadequate or denied responses increased; complaints rose 19% relative to the prior administration, with authorities citing nonexistent information or national-security classification. INAI could not meet because it had four of seven commissioners after López Obrador vetoed two Senate-approved nominees, while further appointments remained pending in the Senate.","notes":["The excerpt does not attribute the appointment blockage specifically to Morena."]}]}
